answer: Apple introduced two new iPhone models in fiscal 2016: the iPhone SE, which began shipping in the third quarter of 2016 [1][4], and the iPhone 7 and 7 Plus, which were introduced in September 2016 [4]. The iPhone SE featured a 4-inch Retina display [4][10], while the iPhone 7 and 7 Plus featured new camera systems, immersive stereo speakers, and water and dust resistance [4].
Apple's manufacturing purchase obligations at the end of fiscal 2026 (September 26, 2026) were $89.7 billion, with $82.7 billion payable within 12 months [1].

Microsoft's revenue growth in Q2 fiscal 2020 (ended December 31, 2019) was driven by strong performance across all three segments. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased 27%, led by Azure growth of 62% [4], and server products and cloud services revenue increased 30% [4]. Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased 17%, driven by Office 365 Commercial growth of 27% and LinkedIn revenue growth of 24% [10]. More Personal Computing revenue increased 2%, driven by Windows revenue growth of 18% [6], offset in part by gaming revenue decline of 21% [5]. Overall, total revenue increased $4.4 billion or 14% [9].
Netflix had 139,259 thousand (139.3 million) paid memberships at the end of 2018 [1]. This represented a 26% increase from the 110.6 million paid memberships at the end of 2017 [1].

As of June 30, 2022, Netflix's total content obligations were $22.8 billion, comprised of $4.2 billion in current content liabilities, $3.0 billion in non-current content liabilities on the balance sheet, and $15.6 billion of obligations not reflected on the balance sheet as they did not meet recognition criteria at that time [1]. Additionally, Netflix estimated unknown future content obligations of approximately $1 billion to $4 billion over the next three years, with most payments expected after the following twelve months [20].

Netflix's international cost of revenues increased in Q3 fiscal 2016 (quarter ending September 30, 2016) primarily due to a $264.6 million increase in content expenses for existing and new streaming content, including more exclusive and original programming [2]. Additionally, other costs rose $32.7 million, mainly from increases in streaming delivery expenses, customer service call center costs, and payment processing fees, all driven by Netflix's growing international member base [2].

NVIDIA's gross margin declined 8.0 percentage points in fiscal 2023 to 56.9%, primarily driven by $2.17 billion of inventory charges related to excess supply of Ampere architecture Gaming and Data Center products, particularly for expected demand in China [16]. The Graphics segment's margin specifically fell due to inventory provisions and lower margins of GeForce GPUs [7], while the Compute & Networking segment also saw margin pressure from inventory provisions [7]. Additionally, NVIDIA implemented pricing programs with Gaming channel partners to address challenging macroeconomic conditions, which reduced gross margin [11].
Tesla had $7.91 billion in outstanding debt at the end of fiscal 2024 (December 31, 2024), of which $2.35 billion was due within the succeeding 12 months [4].

Mark Patterson became Cisco's CFO in fiscal 2025, assuming the role in July 2025 [1]. His background at Cisco spans 25 years: he joined in September 2000 and previously served as Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer from March 2024 to July 2025, Senior Vice President and Chief of Staff to the Chair and CEO from October 2018 to March 2024, Senior Vice President of Strategy, Planning, and Operations for Worldwide Sales and Marketing from July 2015 to October 2018, and held various other leadership and finance roles since 2000 [1].

Cisco was integrating AI into its product portfolios across four key areas during fiscal 2024. The company aimed to simplify how its technology is delivered, managed, and optimized to help customers maximize business value and accelerate digital transformation [1][2]. Specifically, Cisco provided network infrastructure to power AI training and inference workloads for webscalers and enterprises, with high-density routers, switches, and high-performance optics [4]. The company also helped reinvent data center operations by simplifying configuration, monitoring, and maintenance of fabrics, compute, networking, and storage, while delivering differentiated insights from network data to support more informed customer decisions [4].

This expense was related to the application of the transition tax to certain foreign subsidiary earnings generated prior to December 31, 2017, and Oracle expected to settle it periodically over an eight-year period as provided by the Act [9].

Apple's revenue in fiscal 2024 was $391.04 billion [21], up 2% from $383.29 billion in fiscal 2023 [9]. The increase was driven primarily by higher Services revenue, which grew 13% [9], partially offset by declines in iPad and Wearables [9].
Tesla's revenue in Q3 of fiscal 2023 was $23.35 billion [1][6][21]. This represented a 9% increase compared to Q3 of fiscal 2022 [1].
Apple's revenue in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2023 was $89.5 billion [21].
Alphabet had higher net income in fiscal 2022. Alphabet's net income was $59.97 billion [21], while Amazon had a net loss of $2.72 billion [22].
Oracle had more total assets at the end of fiscal 2020. Oracle's total assets were $115.44 billion as of May 31, 2020 [22], compared to Cisco's $94.85 billion as of July 25, 2020 [21].

NVIDIA's revenue grew from $10.92 billion in fiscal 2020 to $130.5 billion in fiscal 2025, a nearly 12-fold increase [7][26]. Year-over-year growth was uneven: revenue rose 53% to $16.68 billion in fiscal 2021 [1], then 61% to $26.91 billion in fiscal 2022 [23], remained flat at $26.97 billion in fiscal 2023 [24], surged 126% to $60.92 billion in fiscal 2024 [25], and accelerated 114% to $130.5 billion in fiscal 2025 [26]. The dramatic acceleration from fiscal 2023 onward was driven by Data Center revenue growth from demand for AI accelerators and the Hopper and Blackwell architectures [2][5].

Alphabet generated $36.0 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2016 [10]. Net cash from operating activities increased from 2015 to 2016 primarily due to increases in cash received from advertising revenues and Google other revenues, offset by increases in cash paid for cost of revenues and operating expenses, with favorable timing of tax payments and refunds also contributing to the increase [1].
Apple's revenue in Q1 fiscal 2025 (ended December 28, 2024) was $124.3 billion [21]. Greater China sales fell 11% to $18.5 billion that quarter due to lower net sales of iPhone [1][2].

Adobe's total revenue in Q2 fiscal 2024 was $5.31 billion [21]. Digital Media revenue grew to $3.91 billion, up 11% year-over-year [1], driven by strong net new user growth [1] and increased revenue from Creative Cloud and Document Cloud subscription offerings due to continued demand in a digital environment, strong engagement across customer segments, and migration of customers to higher-valued subscription offerings with increased revenue per subscription [2].

Amazon had a net loss of $2.72 billion in fiscal 2022 [21]. The International segment's operating loss grew from $924 million in 2021 to $7.75 billion in 2022 [1], primarily due to increased fulfillment and shipping costs from investments in the fulfillment network, higher transportation costs, increased wage rates and incentives, and increased technology and content costs, partially offset by higher advertising sales and increased unit sales [12]. Additionally, foreign currency exchange rates negatively impacted the operating loss by $857 million in 2022 [12].
